contests.office: Soil and Water Conservation District Commission

measures.title: Greenville County Special Sales and Use Tax
measures.summary: Asks whether Greenville County should impose a one percent special sales and use tax for up to eight years, or until $1,100,000,000 has been collected, whichever comes first. Per the ballot question, the money would fund roads, streets, bridges and related drainage ($990,000,000), mass transit operated by or jointly with the county ($33,000,000), and greenbelts such as parks, trails, conservation land and water-quality protection ($77,000,000).
measures.yesMeans: A one percent special sales and use tax is imposed in Greenville County for the listed projects.
measures.noMeans: The one percent special sales and use tax is not imposed.

measures.title: Greenville County General Obligation Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Greenville County may issue up to $150,000,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from the special sales and use tax described in Question 1 and maturing within eight years. The bonds would fund completion of projects in the categories listed in Question 1.
measures.yesMeans: Greenville County may issue up to $150,000,000 in bonds, repaid from the Question 1 sales tax, for those projects.
measures.noMeans: Greenville County may not issue these bonds.

measures.title: City of Greenville One Percent Sales and Use Tax
measures.summary: Asks whether a one percent sales and use tax should be levied in the City of Greenville for no more than eight years, to allow a credit against certain city property (ad valorem) tax liability and to raise a total of $410,145,000. Per the ballot question, the money would go to road, congestion, bridge, intersection and sidewalk projects ($294,279,000), stormwater and drainage ($32,374,000), sewer infrastructure ($41,912,000), public assembly, administration and public safety facilities ($17,580,000), and fire stations ($24,000,000).
measures.yesMeans: A one percent sales and use tax is levied in the City of Greenville for up to eight years for the property tax credit and listed projects.
measures.noMeans: The city one percent sales and use tax is not levied.
